user.title: Grid capacity charge Austria
user.description: Select the grid import energy meter (kWh, total/total_increasing). A live grid import power sensor (W/kW) is optional and improves the forecast. Draft regulation (SNE-G-V), prices are indicative only — the network operator's meter is authoritative.

data_description.energy_entity: Cumulative meter reading of grid import in Wh, kWh or MWh.
data_description.power_entity: Current grid import in W or kW; negative values (export) count as 0.

error.invalid_energy_unit: The energy sensor must use Wh, kWh or MWh.
error.invalid_state_class: The energy sensor must have state_class total or total_increasing.
error.invalid_power_unit: The power sensor must use W or kW.

abort.already_configured: This energy sensor is already configured.

init.title: Thresholds and prices
init.description: Default prices are indicative values (not official); the tariff regulation is still pending. Energy prices of 0 mean 'not set'. Target, tier limit, prices and hysteresis can also be changed directly via the settings entities; changing the plausibility limit reloads the integration.

data_description.tier_limit_kw: Up to and including this value tier 1 applies, above it tier 2 (grid level 7: 10 kW).
data_description.agreed_kw: Contractually agreed grid capacity; existing connections count as 10 kW.
data_description.minimum_kw: At least this much is billed; also at least 20 % of the agreed capacity.
data_description.plausibility_kw: 15-minute averages above this value are treated as measurement errors.
data_description.hysteresis_kw: 'Peak imminent' switches off only when the forecast falls this far below the target.

error.hysteresis_too_large: Hysteresis must be smaller than the target power.
error.target_above_plausibility: Target power must not exceed the plausibility limit.

hysteresis_too_large.message: Hysteresis must be smaller than the target power ({target} kW).

target_above_plausibility.message: Target power must not exceed the plausibility limit ({plausibility} kW).

entry_not_found.message: No Netzentgelt entry with this ID was found.

entry_not_loaded.message: The Netzentgelt entry is not loaded.

path_not_allowed.message: Path "{path}" is not allowed. The file must be inside the Home Assistant configuration directory (no hidden folders) or in a directory listed in allowlist_external_dirs.

invalid_file_type.message: "{path}": only .csv and .txt files can be imported.

file_too_large.message: File "{path}" is too large (at most 20 MB).

no_data.message: "{path}" contains no rows with a timestamp.

no_value_column.message: "{path}": no value column (kW or kWh) found.

decimal_comma_ambiguous.message: "{path}": comma-separated file with decimal commas — the values are ambiguous. Export with ';' as separator or put the values in quotes.

import_load_profile.name: Import load profile
import_load_profile.description: Reads a 15-minute load profile (e.g. the portal export of your grid operator) from a CSV file, adds it to the monthly peak history and the load profile, and imports hourly values into the long-term statistics of the 15-minute power sensor — only for periods before your own measurements.

config_entry_id.name: Entry
config_entry_id.description: The Netzentgelt entry (meter) the load profile belongs to.

path.name: File
path.description: Path of the CSV file relative to the Home Assistant configuration directory, e.g. netzentgelt/lastgang.csv.

timestamp_is_end.name: Timestamp is end
timestamp_is_end.description: Enable if the timestamp marks the end of the quarter hour (default: start, as in the Netz OÖ portal).

overwrite.name: Overwrite own measurement
overwrite.description: Replace the own measurement of a month with the import — only if all own quarter hours of that month lie within the imported period (otherwise merged, see months_overwrite_skipped). Off: the peak is the maximum of both.

import_statistics.name: Import long-term statistics
import_statistics.description: Import hourly mean, minimum and maximum values as statistics of the 15-minute power sensor (only hours before the first existing statistic).
